chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from Sama'ah, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the slaughter of the Jew and the Christian, so he said: 'Do not go near it.'

key_terms.لَا تَقْرَبُوهَا: Do not go near it / Do not approach it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of Jews and Christians according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a concise ruling on the meat of the People of the Book, instructing the seeker not to 'approach' (*la taqrabuha*) their slaughtered animals. While often interpreted as a prohibition (*nahy*) in Shia jurisprudence, the phrasing allows for scholarly discussion regarding whether it denotes absolute impermissibility or strong caution (*karahah*), distinguishing it from the general permissibility granted in Quran 5:5. This narration is central to the debate on whether the specific conditions of Islamic slaughter are required for the meat of Jews and Christians to be considered halal.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Al Magra, from Sama’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> a slaughter by the Jews and the Christians.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not go near it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu al-Mighra’ from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the animals slaughtered by the Jews and Christians. He (the Imam) said, ‘Do not go close to such slaughtered animals.’”
